title: Stalks of O_X-modules commute with kernels, images and cokernels (Stacks 01AG)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] (more generally a ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$), $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (kernels computed sectionwise, cokernels the sheafifications of the sectionwise cokernels), $x\in X$, and stalks, germs and stalk maps $\varphi_x$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with kernel $k:\operatorname{Ker}\varphi\to\mathcal F$, cokernel $c:\mathcal G\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$, and image $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\operatorname{Ker}(c)\subseteq\mathcal G$ with inclusion $\iota$ and the factorization $\varphi=\iota\circ\bar\varphi$, $\bar\varphi:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{Im}\varphi$. Then: (1) if $\varphi_U$ is injective for every open $U$ (e.g. $\varphi$ a monomorphism, or the inclusion of a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module), $\varphi_x$ is injective; (2) $k_x$ is injective with image $\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi_x)$; (3) $c_x$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$, so it induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\mathcal G_x/\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)\cong(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)_x$; (4) $\bar\varphi_x$ is surjective and $\iota_x$ is injective with image $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$, i.e. $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)_x=\operatorname{Im}(\varphi_x)$ as submodules of $\mathcal G_x$; (5) a complex $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is exact at $\mathcal G$ if and only if $\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal H_x$ is exact at $\mathcal G_x$ for every $x\in X$.

proof.text: *Step 0 (conventions).* By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] the stalk map of a morphism $\psi$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is $\psi_x(s_x)=\psi_U(s)_x$; hence $(\psi\circ\chi)_x=\psi_x\circ\chi_x$, $(\mathrm{id})_x=\mathrm{id}$, $0_x=0$, and an isomorphism $u$ has bijective stalk map $u_x$ with inverse $(u^{-1})_x$. Kernels and cokernels in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ are unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with $k$, resp. $c$; by this functoriality, each of (2)-(4) holds for one choice of kernel and cokernel if and only if it holds for every choice. So we may use the following choices. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] the kernel is computed sectionwise: $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi(U)=\{s\in\mathcal F(U):\varphi_U(s)=0\}$ with the restrictions of $\mathcal F$, and $k_U$ the inclusion. Germs: every element of a stalk $\mathcal P_x$ is a germ $s_x$ with $s\in\mathcal P(U)$, $x\in U$, and $s_x=0$ iff $s|_W=0$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

*Step 1 (clause (1)).* Assume $\varphi_U$ is injective for every open $U$. Let $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $x\in U$, with $\varphi_x(s_x)=\varphi_U(s)_x=0$. Then there is an open $x\in W\subseteq U$ with $0=\varphi_U(s)|_W=\varphi_W(s|_W)$ ($\varphi$ commutes with restrictions), so $s|_W=0$ by injectivity of $\varphi_W$, and $s_x=(s|_W)_x=0$. As every element of $\mathcal F_x$ is such a germ, $\varphi_x$ is injective. If $\varphi$ is a monomorphism of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, then $\varphi\circ k=0=\varphi\circ0$ gives $k=0$; since $k_U$ is the inclusion of $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi(U)=\ker\varphi_U$ (Step 0), $\ker\varphi_U=0$, i.e. $\varphi_U$ is injective for every $U$; the inclusion of a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module is injective on sections by definition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Modules, Section 17.3 (lines 102-114); stalk computation written out

proof.text: *Step 2 (clause (2)).* $k$ is injective on every $U$, so $k_x$ is injective by Step 1. Image contained in $\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi_x)$: $\varphi_x\circ k_x=(\varphi\circ k)_x=0$ (Step 0). Conversely let $\sigma\in\mathcal F_x$ with $\varphi_x(\sigma)=0$; write $\sigma=s_x$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. Then $\varphi_U(s)_x=0$, so $\varphi_W(s|_W)=\varphi_U(s)|_W=0$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$, i.e. $s|_W\in\operatorname{Ker}\varphi(W)$, and $\sigma=(s|_W)_x=k_x\big((s|_W)_x\big)$, the germ on the right taken in $(\operatorname{Ker}\varphi)_x$. Hence $k_x$ maps $(\operatorname{Ker}\varphi)_x$ isomorphically onto $\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi_x)$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linearly [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; this is the source's $\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi)_x=\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi_x)$.

*Step 3 (the cokernel as a sheafification).* Let $\mathcal Q$ be the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (the restrictions of $\mathcal G$ carry $\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ into $\varphi_V(\mathcal F(V))$ since $\varphi$ commutes with restrictions, and are semilinear, so they induce semilinear restrictions of $\mathcal Q$), $\pi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q$ the sectionwise quotient map, a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\theta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q^\#$ its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]: $\mathcal Q^\#$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal Q$ as a presheaf of abelian groups, with its $\mathcal O_X$-module structure, $\theta$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear, and every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map from $\mathcal Q$ to a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules factors uniquely through $\theta$. Put $c=\theta\circ\pi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q^\#$. Then $c\circ\varphi=0$ ($\pi_U\circ\varphi_U=0$). $c$ is a cokernel of $\varphi$ in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: if $\beta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\beta\circ\varphi=0$, then each $\beta_U$ vanishes on $\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ and induces an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear $\bar\beta_U:\mathcal Q(U)\to\mathcal H(U)$, compatible with restrictions (since $\beta$ is), so $\bar\beta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal H$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\bar\beta\circ\pi=\beta$, and the universal property gives $\gamma:\mathcal Q^\#\to\mathcal H$ with $\gamma\circ\theta=\bar\beta$, so $\gamma\circ c=\beta$. Uniqueness: if $\gamma\circ c=\gamma'\circ c$, then $\gamma\circ\theta\circ\pi=\gamma'\circ\theta\circ\pi$, and as every $\pi_U$ is surjective, $\gamma\circ\theta=\gamma'\circ\theta$, whence $\gamma=\gamma'$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $\theta$. So we take $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=\mathcal Q^\#$ and this $c$ (Step 0).

proof.text: *Step 4 (stalks of the presheaf cokernel).* $\pi_x:\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal Q_x$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$. Surjective: every element of $\mathcal Q_x$ is a germ $q_x$ with $q\in\mathcal Q(U)$, and $q=\pi_U(g)$ for some $g\in\mathcal G(U)$, so $q_x=\pi_x(g_x)$. $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)\subseteq\ker\pi_x$: $\pi_x\circ\varphi_x=(\pi\circ\varphi)_x=0$ (Step 0). $\ker\pi_x\subseteq\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$: let $g\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $\pi_x(g_x)=\pi_U(g)_x=0$; then there is an open $x\in W\subseteq U$ with $\pi_W(g|_W)=\pi_U(g)|_W=0$ in $\mathcal Q(W)$, i.e. $g|_W=\varphi_W(f)$ for some $f\in\mathcal F(W)$, and $g_x=(g|_W)_x=\varphi_W(f)_x=\varphi_x(f_x)$. All maps are $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

proof.text: *Step 5 (stalks commute with sheafification).* By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\theta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q^\#$ is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal Q$ on the space $X$; so by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] the stalk map $\theta_x:\mathcal Q_x\to\mathcal Q^\#_x$, $q_x\mapsto\theta_U(q)_x$, is a bijective homomorphism of abelian groups. It is the stalk map of the $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\theta$, hence $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so it is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.

source.place: Modules, Section 17.3 (lines 124-127: 'Since taking stalks commutes with taking sheafification, see Sheaves, Lemma 007Z')

proof.text: *Step 6 (clause (3)).* By Step 0, $c_x=\theta_x\circ\pi_x$. By Step 5 $\theta_x$ is bijective and by Step 4 $\pi_x$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$; so $c_x$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$, and by the first isomorphism theorem for $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules it induces an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear isomorphism $\mathcal G_x/\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)\cong(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)_x$, $g_x\bmod\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)\mapsto c_x(g_x)$.

*Step 7 (clause (4)).* $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\operatorname{Ker}(c)$ with $\iota$ the kernel inclusion of $c$. By Step 2 applied to $c$, $\iota_x$ is injective with image $\operatorname{Ker}(c_x)$, which is $\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)$ by Step 6. From $\varphi=\iota\circ\bar\varphi$ and Step 0, $\varphi_x=\iota_x\circ\bar\varphi_x$, so $\iota_x(\bar\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x))=\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)=\iota_x((\operatorname{Im}\varphi)_x)$; as $\iota_x$ is injective, $\bar\varphi_x(\mathcal F_x)=(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)_x$, i.e. $\bar\varphi_x$ is surjective. Thus $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)_x=\operatorname{Im}(\varphi_x)$ as submodules of $\mathcal G_x$ via $\iota_x$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AG (label lemma-abelian, lines 149-172: the stalks of image and coimage are the image and coimage of the stalk map)

proof.text: *Step 8 (clause (5)).* Let $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\chi}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\psi}\mathcal H$ be a complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $\psi\circ\chi=0$. For every $x$, $\psi_x\circ\chi_x=(\psi\circ\chi)_x=0$ (Step 0), so $\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal H_x$ is a complex of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules, and it is exact at $\mathcal G_x$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] iff $\ker\psi_x\subseteq\chi_x(\mathcal F_x)$ (image and kernel in the category of modules being the set-theoretic ones). By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2), the complex is exact at $\mathcal G$ iff (L): for every open $W$ and $g\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\psi_W(g)=0$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and $f_i\in\mathcal F(W_i)$ with $\chi_{W_i}(f_i)=g|_{W_i}$. (L) $\Rightarrow$ stalkwise exact: let $\gamma\in\mathcal G_x$ with $\psi_x(\gamma)=0$; write $\gamma=g_x$, $g\in\mathcal G(U)$; then $\psi_U(g)|_W=\psi_W(g|_W)=0$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$; apply (L) to $g|_W$ and pick $i$ with $x\in W_i$: $\gamma=(g|_{W_i})_x=\chi_{W_i}(f_i)_x=\chi_x((f_i)_x)$. Stalkwise exact $\Rightarrow$ (L): let $g\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\psi_W(g)=0$. For each $x\in W$, $\psi_x(g_x)=\psi_W(g)_x=0$, so $g_x=\chi_x(\phi)$ for some $\phi\in\mathcal F_x$; write $\phi=f_x$ with $f\in\mathcal F(U)$, $x\in U$; then $g_x=\chi_U(f)_x$, so there is an open $x\in W_x\subseteq W\cap U$ with $g|_{W_x}=\chi_U(f)|_{W_x}=\chi_{W_x}(f|_{W_x})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The $W_x$, $x\in W$, cover $W$, and $f_x:=f|_{W_x}$ are the required sections. Hence the complex is exact at $\mathcal G$ iff it is exact at $\mathcal G_x$ for every $x\in X$.

split_report.summary: Split following Modules Section 17.3 and Lemma 01AG in 9 steps: conventions (sectionwise kernel, functoriality of stalk maps, independence of the choice of kernel/cokernel); (1) and (2) by germ computations; the cokernel as the module sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel, with its cokernel property checked from the universal property (Sheaves 0089); stalks of the presheaf cokernel by germs; stalks commute with sheafification (Sheaves 007Z, existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space); (3) by composition; (4) from (2) applied to the cokernel map and (3); (5) from the reviewed local-lifting criterion lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting (2) plus germ computations in both directions. No new nodes. Added def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence to stmt_deps (clause (5) uses exactness). lean.statement: theorem module_stalk_exact (X : RingedSpace.{u}) {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)} (φ : F ⟶ G) : ((∀ (U : Opens X), Function.Injective (ConcreteCategory.hom (φ.val.app (Opposite.op U)))) → ∀ (x : X), Mono ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map φ)) ∧ (∀ (x : X), Mono ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (kernel.ι φ)) ∧ ((ShortComplex.mk ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (kernel.ι φ)) ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map φ) (by rw [← (moduleStalkFunctor X x).map_comp] simp)).Exact)) ∧ (∀ (x : X), Epi ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (cokernel.π φ)) ∧ ((ShortComplex.mk ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map φ) ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (cokernel.π φ)) (by rw [← (moduleStalkFunctor X x).map_comp] simp)).Exact)) ∧ (∀ (x : X), Epi ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (Abelian.factorThruImage φ)) ∧ Mono ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (Abelian.image.ι φ)) ∧ LinearMap.range ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map (Abelian.image.ι φ)).hom = LinearMap.range ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).map φ).hom) ∧ (∀ (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (χ : F ⟶ G) (ψ : G ⟶ H), ∀ (h : χ ≫ ψ = 0), (ShortComplex.mk χ ψ h).Exact ↔ ∀ (x : X), ((ShortComplex.mk χ ψ h).map (moduleStalkFunctor X x)).Exact)
